centered-data-matrix.t: **Xc** is the centered data matrix: one row per customer, one column per feature. From here, two routes lead to the same principal directions.

covariance-route.t: The first route forms the small symmetric matrix **S = XcᵀXc / (n − 1)**. It summarizes all the spread in the data in a 2 × 2 table.

eigen-route.t: Take the eigen-decomposition of S: eigenvalues **6.03 and 0.17**, and eigenvectors **v₁ and v₂**. The eigenvectors are the principal directions.

svd-route.t: The second route factors **Xc directly** as **U Σ Vᵀ**, without ever forming the covariance matrix. Software often prefers this because it is numerically safer.

u-sigma-vt.t: **U** (6 × 2) holds normalized scores, **Σ** (2 × 2) the singular values, and **Vᵀ** (2 × 2) the directions. Multiplying them rebuilds Xc.

principal-directions.t: The first row is **PC1 = (0.754, 0.657)**. The second row comes out as (0.657, −0.754), the **opposite sign** of the eigenvector v₂. A whole row can flip sign and still describe the same axis.

singular-values.t: Σ holds **5.49 and 0.93**. Squaring them and dividing by n − 1 gives **6.03 and 0.17**, the same eigenvalues as before.

same-pc1.t: Both routes give the same first direction, **(0.754, 0.657)**, and the same variance. A program may print the opposite sign, but it is the same axis.

compare-methods.t: **PCA is the analysis; SVD is a tool that gets you there.** Libraries prefer SVD because it avoids forming XcᵀXc, which can lose numerical precision.
